clue.text: Top of gas cooker is cracked

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter, so only the opening letter of gas is used

parts.note: an Aga is a brand of large cast-iron range cooker, a fixture of British country kitchens

explanation.surface: Someone warns that the gas cooker's hob has a crack in it.
explanation.walkthrough: AGA is a heavy British range cooker. 'Top of' takes the first letter of 'gas', G.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal slang for mad or crazy, as in going soft in the head.

clue.text: Rotten holiday faced by batsman

parts.note: food that has gone off is rotten
a break is a short holiday

explanation.surface: A cricketer's miserable holiday is described alongside a batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an off-break is a ball spun by the bowler so that it turns in towards the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a type of cricket delivery, so it is something a batsman has to face from the bowler.

clue.text: Courage? King George has it!

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George, as seen on old postboxes
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether courage is a royal quality and says King George has plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit means determined courage and toughness in the face of hardship, a near synonym.

clue.text: Mad about Mickey, almost deserted

indicators.note: Mad is placed about, that is around, the next piece in this clue

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the actor's surname is cut off

parts.note: Mickey Rooney was the American film actor

explanation.surface: A fan crazy about Mickey Rooney is nearly abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: Mickey Rooney was a Hollywood actor; 'almost' drops his surname's last letter and 'about' wraps the word Mad around what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stranded and left alone, as on a desert island, has been abandoned there.

clue.text: Could be so slim and supple

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters of so slim might become another word if rearranged

explanation.surface: A dieter hopes to become slender and flexible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' rearranges the letters of SO SLIM. 'and' is the link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lissom describes a body that is slim, graceful and flexible, the same as lithe or supple.

clue.text: For cleaning clothes, Gandhi's way is wrong

indicators.note: a way that is wrong is all mixed up, so these letters must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone declares that Gandhi's method of doing the laundry is mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is wrong' rearranges the letters of GANDHIS WAY; here the S of the possessive counts as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The washing day is the day of the week set aside for laundering a household's garments.

clue.text: Loan shark certain to be found in the old city

indicators.note: one piece is placed within another, as something found inside a place

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia, the standard crossword old city
certain means sure

explanation.surface: A predatory lender is surely lurking in some ancient metropolis.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur, in ancient Mesopotamia, is the crossword's favourite old city; 'to be found in' sets the word for certain inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurer lends money at exorbitant interest, just as a loan shark does.

clue.text: Fed up with unknown challenge

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word Fed is written from bottom to top

parts.note: in algebra x, y and z are the unknowns, so y stands for an unknown

explanation.surface: Someone sick of an anonymous opponent mounts a challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FED into DEF in this down clue; 'with' joins on Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To defy someone is to openly resist or dare them, which is a verb meaning to challenge.

clue.text: In my judgement, it's the skyline

definitions.meaning: a phrase meaning in my opinion, from where I stand
the horizon is the furthest point the eye can reach

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is read twice: once as an idiom for 'in my opinion', once literally as the limit of one's vision, which the skyline marks.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in my view; read literally it marks the limit of one's sight, the horizon.

clue.text: See 9
Sea bird seen on a golf course

definitions.meaning: a large ocean-going bird with a huge wingspan
in golf, a score of three under par on a hole

explanation.walkthrough: In golf, birdie, eagle and albatross name scores of one, two and three under par.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a large wandering ocean bird and, in golf, a score three strokes under par.

clue.text: Thomas puts dried grass over road

indicators.note: the dried grass is put over the road, enclosing it within this across entry

parts.note: hay is grass cut and dried for fodder

explanation.surface: A man named Thomas lays out hay on top of a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' lays the grass across the road, enclosing it. Thomas Hardy was the English novelist and poet of Wessex.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hardy wrote Tess of the d'Urbervilles, so the first name points to that surname.

clue.text: Tar gets nose broken in mutiny

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so these letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written, though on the surface a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor has his nose broken in a shipboard rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges TAR and NOSE together; 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is betrayal of one's sovereign or state, a revolt akin to mutiny against authority.

clue.text: Beverage given to child in school

parts.note: tea is a common hot beverage

explanation.surface: A drink is handed to a pupil at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' here is the verb, to instruct; 'given to' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to train or instruct them, the same as to teach them.

clue.text: Shows that can be seen through

definitions.meaning: a pair of glasses, lenses you look through

explanation.definitionFit: The word means impressive displays or shows, and also glasses worn to see through.

clue.text: Martine converted in this tower

indicators.note: converted means changed into a different form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman named Martine is converted to a new faith inside a tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' rearranges MARTINE; 'converted' nods to religion, since the tower belongs to a mosque.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque from which the call to prayer is made.

clue.text: Boy Scouts left holding nothing up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole construction is read from bottom to top
holding means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Scouts who were abandoned are holding up nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts O inside PORT to make POORT, and 'up' turns it over to read TROOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is the unit into which Boy Scouts are organised under a scoutmaster.

clue.text: Not known to be dipped in beer in this joint

indicators.note: something dipped in a drink goes inside it, so one piece enters the other

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
NK is the abbreviation for not known

explanation.surface: Something unknown gets dunked in a pint at this bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be dipped in' sinks the abbreviation into the beer; 'in this' is only the link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the joint connecting the foot to the leg.

clue.text: Enjoy what Alan Titchmarsh does?

definitions.meaning: Alan Titchmarsh is a well-known British TV gardener, who turns over soil

explanation.walkthrough: Alan Titchmarsh is a famous British television gardener; the question mark flags the playful second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig something is slang for liking it, and a gardener digs with a spade.

clue.text: Safe journey once ocean's shadow is lifted

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the pieces are raised and read from bottom to top

parts.note: the deep is the ocean, and the possessive adds S
to dog someone is to shadow or follow them

explanation.surface: A traveller is wished well once the ocean's dark shade clears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is lifted' raises the whole run in this down entry, so it reads from the bottom up; 'once' is just a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a traditional wish for a safe journey and success, said to someone departing.

clue.text: One teetotaller will break up a party as before

indicators.note: the two pieces break into the party, splitting it apart

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
I is the Roman numeral for one
TT stands for teetotal, a non-drinker

explanation.surface: A lone non-drinker threatens to spoil a party, just as last time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will break up' splits the party open so the one and the non-drinker sit inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto is used to mean the same again, repeating what was said above or before.

clue.text: Tollgate muddled up tinker

indicators.note: muddled means jumbled up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A travelling tinker gets confused at a toll barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muddled' rearranges the letters of UP TINKER.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnpike is a road barrier where a toll is collected, hence a tollgate.

clue.text: Something worn outside a bit, or in the house

indicators.note: the first piece goes outside the second, enclosing it

parts.note: a hat is something worn on the head
taken as written

explanation.surface: A garment goes on the outside a little, or perhaps indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps HAT around A BIT: H-ABIT-AT. 'or in the' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural home of a creature, so the place that houses it.

clue.text: Boy nearly bought one in Colombia

indicators.note: nearly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
to get something is to acquire or buy it, so got means bought
a means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A lad almost bought a souvenir while visiting Colombia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' loses the last letter of Boy; the definition leans on Bogota being the capital of Colombia.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogota is the capital city of Colombia, so it is a place found there.

clue.text: Repeated knocks make Irish twins retreat

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so the doubled name is read backwards
twins means the name appears twice over

parts.note: Pat is a stock name for an Irishman, from Patrick

explanation.surface: Someone sends a pair of Irish twins packing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twins' doubles PAT to PATPAT and 'retreat' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled word imitates the sound of light repeated knocks on a door.

clue.text: Doris needs advice about right outing

parts.note: Doris Day was the American singer and actress

indicators.note: about means the advice goes around the next letter

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice

explanation.surface: Doris needs guidance on the correct excursion.
explanation.walkthrough: Doris Day was an American singer and film star; 'about' puts the advice around the letter for right.
explanation.definitionFit: A day trip is a journey made for pleasure there and back in one day, an excursion.

clue.text: A little smoke in the morning round is wonderful

indicators.note: turning round reverses the order of the letters

parts.note: a cig is a cigarette, a small smoke
AM is ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: Having a quick cigarette before work is marvellous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns the smoke and the morning letters back to front as one run, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Magic as an informal adjective means excellent, marvellous or wonderful.

clue.text: Masses of writing about ex-pupil

indicators.note: the writing goes about, that is around, the other piece

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing
OB is old boy, a former pupil of a school

explanation.surface: Lots of writing is about a former schoolboy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' means the writing abbreviation surrounds the ex-pupil; old boy is the British term for a former pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: Mobs are disorderly crowds or masses of people.

clue.text: West Indian dish gives energy to each belly

parts.note: pep means vigour or energy
per means each, as in so much per head
a pot or pot belly is a large stomach

explanation.surface: A Caribbean meal is said to put a spring in each paunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives' and 'to' are link words joining PEP, PER and POT.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperpot is a spicy Caribbean stew of meat and vegetables, a classic West Indian dish.

clue.text: Poet fails to start the food

indicators.note: a word that fails to start loses its first letter

parts.note: John Keats was the English Romantic poet

explanation.surface: A writer of verse cannot begin his meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fails to start' drops the K from KEATS. 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal for food, as in grabbing some eats.

clue.text: This PM's not for turning — lady's conclusion

indicators.note: a word for turning is reversed, so not is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its last letter, here of lady's

explanation.surface: Echoes Margaret Thatcher's famous line that the lady was not for turning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for turning' reverses NOT to TON, and 'conclusion' takes Y from 'lady's'. Tony Blair was a UK Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Blair was Labour prime minister, so the forename identifies that PM.

clue.text: Similarly, the money basket is fluctuating

indicators.note: something fluctuating keeps changing, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that the value of a basket of currencies is going up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is fluctuating' rearranges the fourteen letters of THE MONEY BASKET.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means likewise, introducing a point that follows the same logic.

clue.text: See 31
